This Wave extended the seeded validator with a validate-dir mode and closed-schema enforcement; another writer has also changed both files on the base branch, so a merge will conflict there rather than compose.
collision_events.effect_detail: Nothing was lost or overwritten. This branch was never merged, rebased or pushed anywhere but itself, and no sibling branch's content was read or incorporated. The collision is latent and will surface at merge time.
collision_events.resolution_detail: Resolving it would mean reading and reconciling another writer's work, which is outside this worker's boundary and would risk destroying their result. The overlap is reported instead.

collision_count_note: One latent path-overlap collision with the PR base branch, covering 17 paths. Recorded as 0 in the first draft of this record, which was measured only within this branch. Zero collisions inside a single writer's own branch is not a collision-free estate.
collision_detection_method: Within this branch: single-writer invariant plus `git status --porcelain` inspection before each commit. Across the estate: path-set intersection between this branch's diff and the base branch's diff from the shared branch point, measured at the end of the Wave and pinned to the base head sha above so it is re-checkable.
collision_detection_gap: The intersection was measured once, at the end. Nothing detected it while the Wave was running, so a genuine concurrent overwrite would not have been noticed until the same end-of-wave check. A live collision detector remains NOT_YET.

worktree_isolation.reason: Isolated worktrees exist to separate concurrent writers. Wave A had exactly one writer, so no isolation boundary was needed. Isolated worktrees or separate cloud VMs remain the correct mechanism if a future wave runs concurrent subordinate writers, and are recorded as available-but-unused in workstreams/po03/evidence/scale-ladder.json.
